clause_text: This Regulation applies to the processing of personal data in the context of the activities of an establishment of a controller or a processor in the Union.
For the purposes of this Regulation, 'personal data' means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ('data subject').
For the purposes of this Regulation, 'controller' is defined as the natural or legal person which determines the purposes and means of the processing.
General definitions and background context regarding cross-border data transfers are purely informative.
Scope and applicability of internal compliance documentation guidelines across the organization.
The controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where the personal data are no longer necessary.
The controller and the processor must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.
In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay notify the supervisory authority.
Processing by a processor shall be governed by a binding contract that is required to set out the subject-matter and duration.
Each controller must maintain a written record of processing activities under its responsibility.
The controller and the processor shall designate a data protection officer whenever required by law.
Where a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk, the controller shall, where relevant, carry out an assessment of the impact.
Where Article 3(2) applies, the controller or processor shall designate in writing a representative, if applicable.
When the personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk, the controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject where appropriate.
The controller shall consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where relevant if an impact assessment indicates unmitigated risk.
The Member States and supervisory authorities may encourage the drawing up of codes of conduct intended to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation.
The Member States and Commission should consider establishing data protection certification mechanisms and seals.
Independent certification bodies are encouraged to provide periodic audit reviews upon request.
